313:static std::string monitorsRequest(eHyprCtlOutputFormat format, std::string request) {
314:    CVarList vars(request, 0, ' ');
315:    auto     allMonitors = false;
316:
317:    if (vars.size() > 2)
318:        return "too many args";
319:
320:    if (vars.size() == 2 && vars[1] == "all")
321:        allMonitors = true;
322:
323:    std::string result = "";
324:    if (format == eHyprCtlOutputFormat::FORMAT_JSON) {
325:        result += "[";
326:
327:        for (auto const& m : allMonitors ? State::monitorState()->allMonitors() : State::monitorState()->monitors()) {
328:            result += CHyprCtl::getMonitorData(m, format);
329:        }
330:
331:        trimTrailingComma(result);
332:
333:        result += "]";
334:    } else {
335:        for (auto const& m : allMonitors ? State::monitorState()->allMonitors() : State::monitorState()->monitors()) {
336:            if (!m->m_output || m->m_id == -1)
337:                continue;
338:
339:            result += CHyprCtl::getMonitorData(m, format);
340:        }
341:    }
342:
343:    return result;
344:}

== Hyprland-Parser.cpp:110-143 ==
110:bool CMonitorRuleParser::parseMode(const std::string& value) {
111:    if (value.empty() || value.starts_with("pref"))
112:        m_rule.m_resolution = Vector2D();
113:    else if (value.starts_with("highrr"))
114:        m_rule.m_resolution = Vector2D(-1, -1);
115:    else if (value.starts_with("highres"))
116:        m_rule.m_resolution = Vector2D(-1, -2);
117:    else if (value.starts_with("maxwidth"))
118:        m_rule.m_resolution = Vector2D(-1, -3);
119:    else if (parseModeLine(value, m_rule.m_drmMode)) {
120:        m_rule.m_resolution  = Vector2D(m_rule.m_drmMode.hdisplay, m_rule.m_drmMode.vdisplay);
121:        m_rule.m_refreshRate = sc<float>(m_rule.m_drmMode.vrefresh) / 1000;
122:    } else {
123:
124:        if (!value.contains("x")) {
125:            m_error += "invalid resolution ";
126:            m_rule.m_resolution = Vector2D();
127:            return false;
128:        } else {
129:            try {
130:                m_rule.m_resolution.x = stoi(value.substr(0, value.find_first_of('x')));
131:                m_rule.m_resolution.y = stoi(value.substr(value.find_first_of('x') + 1, value.find_first_of('@')));
132:
133:                if (value.contains("@"))
134:                    m_rule.m_refreshRate = stof(value.substr(value.find_first_of('@') + 1));
135:            } catch (...) {
136:                m_error += "invalid resolution ";
137:                m_rule.m_resolution = Vector2D();
138:                return false;
139:            }
140:        }
141:    }
142:    return true;
143:}

== hyprutils-String.cpp:46-86 ==
46:bool Hyprutils::String::isNumber(const std::string& str, bool allowfloat) {
47:    return isNumber2(str, allowfloat);
48:}
49:
50:bool Hyprutils::String::isNumber2(const std::string_view& str, bool allowfloat) {
51:    if (str.empty())
52:        return false;
53:
54:    bool decimalParsed = false;
55:
56:    for (size_t i = 0; i < str.length(); ++i) {
57:        const char& c = str.at(i);
58:
59:        if (i == 0 && str.at(i) == '-') {
60:            // only place where we allow -
61:            continue;
62:        }
63:
64:        if (!isdigit(c)) {
65:            if (!allowfloat)
66:                return false;
67:
68:            if (c != '.')
69:                return false;
70:
71:            if (i == 0)
72:                return false;
73:
74:            if (decimalParsed)
75:                return false;
76:
77:            decimalParsed = true;
78:
79:            continue;
80:        }
81:    }
82:
83:    return isdigit(str.back()) != 0;
84:}
85:
86:void Hyprutils::String::replaceInString(std::string& string, const std::string& what, const std::string& to) {

== wiki-Monitors.md:5-30 ==
5:
6:## General
7:
8:The general config of a monitor looks like this:
9:
10:```ini
11:monitor = name, resolution, position, scale
12:```
13:
14:A common example:
15:
16:```ini
17:monitor = DP-1, 1920x1080@144, 0x0, 1
18:```
19:
20:This will make the monitor on `DP-1` a `1920x1080` display, at
21:144Hz, `0x0` off from the top left corner, with a scale of 1 (unscaled).
22:
23:To list all available monitors (active and inactive):
24:
25:```bash
26:hyprctl monitors all
27:```
28:
29:Monitors are positioned on a virtual "layout". The `position` is the position,
30:in pixels, of said display in the layout. (calculated from the top-left corner)

== wiki-Monitors.md:248-258 ==
248:
249:```ini
250:monitor = eDP-1, 2880x1800@90, 0x0, 1, bitdepth, 10, cm, hdr, sdrbrightness, 1.2, sdrsaturation, 0.98
251:```
252:
253:The default transfer function assumed to be in use on an SDR display for sRGB content is defined by `, sdr_eotf, X`. The default (`0`) is to follow `render:cm_sdr_eotf`. This can be changed to piecewise sRGB with `1`, or  Gamma 2.2 with `2`.
254:
255:### ICC Profiles
256:
257:You can load an icc profile via `, icc, /path/to/icc.icm` (or `icc = path` in v2).
258:

16:Fenced code blocks of the entry, README and lesson are removed before any line is matched. The entry is admitted
17:iff every clause holds:
18:  a  ENTRY exists at REV and is absent at BASE (present at BASE is a setup error, exit 2);
19:  b  within its first 20 raw lines, outside fences: >= 4 distinct `source: S###` lines, exactly one
20:     `verified-at: DATE` and exactly one `recheck:` (ISO date, `NNd` or `on-*`); no such line elsewhere; no
21:     `S###` token anywhere in the entry that is not a cited id;
22:  c  every cited id has exactly one Registry row (0-3 leading spaces), 11 cells, status `mined`, a valid recheck
23:     cell, and used-by listing ENTRY; ids absent at BASE (>= 3) carry opened DATE and a location (last token of
24:     cell 1) holding `/` and `.`; ids present at BASE keep cells 1-9 byte-equal and every BASE used-by item;
25:  d  LESSON `## Gate` holds per cited id exactly one column-0 line `GATE <id> receipt=<path> sha256=<hex>
26:     quote="<q>"` (none outside that section); the receipt is a 100644 file under FETCH at REV with that sha256,
27:     >= 256 bytes; distinct path, sha256 and quote per id; a receipt whose file name is one of PINS must be at
28:     FETCH/<name> with exactly the pinned sha256 - held ids included; a new id's receipt must be one of PINS; the
29:     quote is 3-25 words, occurs exactly once in its receipt's normalized text at word boundaries, also with
30:     comments removed (C/C++ `//`,`/* */`; `#` in .py/.conf), and in no other cited receipt;
31:  e  each new id's location occurs in no other row whose scope cell (cell 5) equals its own, and its last path
32:     component and the receipt name contain one another; a `Hyprland-` receipt's location starts with the
33:     efb50993 raw URL; for every cited id gated on a PINS receipt the location is exactly that pin's URL; a new
34:     row's anchor cell names the receipt with `<name>:<a>[-<b>]` ranges inside the receipt's line count;
35:  f  corpus/README.md holds exactly one column-0 index row for ENTRY;
36:  g  per cited id one entry line names that id and no other, carries its Gate quote and the computed locator
37:     `<receipt name>:<N>` (N = the receipt line where the quote starts); EVERY unfenced line naming a cited id
38:     (other than its `source:` line) carries that id's quote and locator; only the exact census line of h is
39:     exempt from these line checks;
40:  h  monitor census: from the pins the counter computes the rule's default refresh (MonitorRule.hpp
41:     `m_refreshRate = <R>;`), the requested-mode closeness bound (Monitor.cpp `!DELTALESSTHAN(bestMode->refreshRate
42:     / 1000.f, RULE->m_refreshRate, <T>)`), the scale step (Monitor.cpp `std::round(m_scale * <K>.0)`), the search
43:     length (the first `for (size_t i = 1; i < <N>; ++i)` loop after that line; steps = N - 1), the JSON refresh
44:     decimals (HyprCtl.cpp `"refreshRate": {:.<P>f}`) and the number of `ARGS[argno] == "` keys in handleMonitor
45:     (from its signature line to the first following line that is exactly `}`); the entry carries, verbatim,
46:     unfenced and exactly once, `hyprland monitor-rule default_refresh=<R> refresh_tolerance=<T> scale_step=1/<K>
47:     scale_search=<N-1> json_refresh_decimals=<P> line_keys=<n>`, and no other entry line carries one of those six
48:     `name=` tokens with another value;
49:  i  no cited row and no entry line holds a BAD_LOC marker; the Gate receipts of the cited ids cover every name in
50:     PINS;
51:  j  surface coverage: for each SURFACES item (pinned receipt, anchor text that occurs exactly once in it, keyword)
52:     the counter computes the anchor's line L, and some unfenced entry line outside the first 20 raw lines carries
53:     a locator `<receipt>:<a>[-<b>]` with a <= L <= b (b = a when absent) and b - a <= 30, and matches the keyword
54:     (case-insensitive). The seventeen surfaces: parseMode, parsePosition, parseScale (Parser.cpp); handleMonitor
55:     and its invalid-syntax return (legacy ConfigManager.cpp); add's erase and get's reverse search
56:     (MonitorRuleManager.cpp); the 60 Hz default (MonitorRule.hpp); matchesStaticSelector, the closeness bound and
57:     the 1/120 scale search (Monitor.cpp); the JSON refreshRate field and the `all` argument (HyprCtl.cpp); the
58:     explicit-position move (MonitorPositionController.cpp); isNumber2 (String.cpp); the wiki's line format and
59:     its `sdr_eotf` sentence (wiki-Monitors.md).
60:Final line: `PRED-C2-r45: admitted=N/1 verdict=TARGET_MET|TARGET_MISSED rev=<full hash>`; exit 0 iff admitted=1/1,
61:else 1; setup failure exit 2.
62:Residuals (declared): the pins are the trust root; a true quote at a true locator can stand beside a claim it does
63:not support, and a decision table naming no id is not bound (the non-author reading); registry cells 3-6 of a new
64:row are not read except the scope cell and the anchor ranges; clause j binds a locator and a keyword per surface,
65:not the truth of the sentence around them; the census line is bookkeeping of pinned bytes.
